title: Instruction List: arithmetic, comparison and a jump on a rising edge
summary: Keep a running total in an INT variable, add to it on each press with ADD and a conditional jump, and turn it into three BOOL results with LT, EQ and GT.
scope: Passing means your program behaved correctly in the simulator on this computer. It says nothing about a real machine, its timing or its safety, and it does not show the range of a real sensor or the overflow behaviour of a particular controller.
objectives: Use ADD on a number in the current result, and LT, EQ and GT to turn a number into a BOOL.
Skip a group of lines with JMPCN so that a number changes only on the rising edge of an input.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: In src/TypedSteps.il the three comparisons at the end are written: LD Total loads the INT, LT 10 compares it and leaves a BOOL, and ST Low stores it. Write the arithmetic above them: on each rising edge of Step add 5 to Total, and while Reset is TRUE set Total to 0.
stages.checkpoint: Total goes 0, 5, 10, 15, and the three outputs show which band it is in.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: Step is pressed three times, the first press lasting two scans. Predict which output is ON at {{t:20}}, {{t:40}} and {{t:60}} ms.
stages.checkpoint: {{v:TypedSteps.Low=true,TypedSteps.Exact=false,TypedSteps.High=false@20|Low}} at {{t:20}} ms (Total is 5); {{v:TypedSteps.Low=false,TypedSteps.Exact=true,TypedSteps.High=false@40|Exact}} at {{t:40}} ms (Total is 10); {{v:TypedSteps.Low=false,TypedSteps.Exact=false,TypedSteps.High=true@60|High}} at {{t:60}} ms (Total is 15).

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Correct the starting program, save it, then press {{ui:learn.check}}. The starter remembers Step in StepWas and writes the three comparisons, but never changes Total, so Low stays ON for ever. Change it so that each press of Step adds 5 to Total once, however long the press lasts, and Total goes back to 0 while Reset is TRUE. Write the instructions yourself: the declarations and the three comparisons are already there.
stages.checkpoint: {{ui:learn.check}} reports the scenario of this lesson as passed.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press {{ui:learn.check}}. ZPLC runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson and lists every assertion that failed.
stages.checkpoint: The scenario is named TypedSteps and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Compare {{t:20}}, {{t:40}} and {{t:60}} ms: exactly one of the three outputs is ON each time, and Reset at {{t:80}} ms brings Low back.
stages.checkpoint: Exact is ON only at the one total of 10, from {{t:40}} ms; the long first press added 5 once, not twice.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: What happens if you write Exact with GE 10? And if the condition of the addition uses Step alone, without the value of StepWas from the previous scan? Try each and see which assertion fails.
stages.checkpoint: A comparison leaves a BOOL in the current result, and EQ is not the same as GE. Without the previous value of Step a press that lasts two scans adds twice. The scenario only watches the three BOOL outputs; it does not show the value of Total itself or what happens when an INT overflows.

hints.text: Look at the first lines: StepWas takes the value of Step before any condition could read the value of the previous scan, and no line loads Total or adds to it.

LD Step, ANDN StepWas, JMPCN skip, LD Total, ADD 5, ST Total, skip:, then the lines that copy Step to StepWas, then LD Reset, JMPCN keep, LD 0, ST Total, keep:, before the three comparisons. JMPCN jumps to its label when the current result is FALSE, so the lines between are skipped.

faultCases: The starter remembers Step in StepWas and writes the three comparisons, but never changes Total, so Low stays ON for ever.
